topic: Someone finds their partner's bucket list
text: The rain was just a drizzle tonight, barely enough to gloss the streets, but it didn’t stop her from showing up at my door, soaking through to the bones. She had a piece of paper clutched in her hand, the edges curling from the wet. “It’s his bucket list,” she said, as if that explained everything. I took the paper, let the light from my desk lamp play over the items scribbled in ink—skydiving, visiting Machu Picchu, writing a novel. Things a younger version of him might've wanted, before he got too comfortable, too predictable. “He never told me this existed,” she whispered, more to herself. I folded the list, slipped it into an envelope. “People keep secrets, even from the ones closest to them,” I said, offering her a towel. “Sometimes, these lists are just Dreams left behind, markers in time. Let’s see what your man’s really been up to.”
